message.content:
Since \((5,0)\) and \((4,3)\) have the same length, the reflection line is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them.

The midpoint is
\[
\left(\frac{5+4}{2},\frac{0+3}{2}\right)=\left(\frac92,\frac32\right).
\]
The line through the origin and this midpoint has slope
\[
\frac{3/2}{9/2}=\frac13,
\]
so the reflection line is \(y=\frac13x\), i.e. direction vector \((3,1)\).

For a reflection across the line spanned by unit vector \(u\), the formula is
\[
R(v)=2(u\cdot v)u-v.
\]
Here
\[
u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3,1).
\]
For \(v=(-2,3)\),
\[
u\cdot v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(-6+3)=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}.
\]
Thus
\[
R(v)=2\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right)\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3,1)-(-2,3)
\]
\[
=2\left(-\frac{3}{10}\right)(3,1)-(-2,3)
\]
\[
=\left(-\frac95,-\frac35\right)-(-2,3)
\]
\[
=\left(\frac15,-\frac{18}{5}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix} \frac15 \\[2pt] -\frac{18}{5} \end{pmatrix}\).
